summary: Ambitious Impact's 2021 estimate for a new charity doing exploratory cause-prioritisation research, to find and promote new cause areas and interventions for effective altruist and other donors. The idea CEARCH (the Centre for Exploratory Altruism Research) was founded to run in 2022. A re-implementation of AIM's spreadsheet, traced from its five-year benefit-cost ratio, in dollars of current effective-altruist donations' worth of value per dollar spent; our bridge values each such dollar at the site's shared value of a dollar moved, from where effective donors give and each destination's live result. Ambitious Impact notes that 'this CEA is only comparable to other CEAs created for EA meta charities by Charity Entrepreneurship'.

rows.label: Total costs over the years modelled
rows.explainer: Costs start at $150,000 and grow 20% a year: $150,000 × (1.2⁵ − 1) / 0.2 = $1,116,240 over five years. The sheet caps growth after 8 years, which doesn't bind at 5.

rows.label: Average cost per year
Benefit-cost ratio over the years modelled
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact's bottom line: value created over five years, in dollars of today's top-tier effective-altruist donations, per dollar spent. The report gives the third year as an example, 'Leverage ratio ~8'. The sheet's note (CEA!F17:J17) places it between a fundraising organisation's money moved per dollar (4:1) and a successful think tank's (10:1 or more), with no source for either.

rows.label: Value of benefits that come a year after the costs
rows.explainer: The sheet's benefits start a year after its costs (its 'impact delayed by 1 year') and both are summed undiscounted. We discount the benefits by that lag at the shared discount rate (Your values); the evaluator view pins it to 0, as the sheet has it.

rows.label: Method 2's lasting impact, discounted for time as well
rows.formula: 1 - method2_impact_used * method2_weight / (method1_impact_used * method1_weight + method2_impact_used * method2_weight) * (1 - idea1_replaceability / (idea1_replaceability + $discount_rate))
rows.explainer: Method 2 values each idea's yearly impact as a perpetuity that shrinks by 15% a year, the chance someone else would do the work later (the same 15% for all three ideas): yearly impact ÷ 0.15. Time preference would shrink it further, to yearly impact ÷ (0.15 + the discount rate). This applies that to method 2's share of the weighted impact (about 55%); method 1 is unaffected. At the evaluator view's 0% it is 1.

rows.label: Chance the new organisation succeeds
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency. The sheet assumes the organisation succeeds ('did not discount for chance of organizational failure', CEA!D61), because its comparison organisations (ACE, GiveWell, Rethink Priorities) are ones that succeeded. Every not-yet-proven meta organisation on the site gets one shared chance of success in our view: Ambitious Impact's own average of three methods for a new evaluator, 55.7% (range 50–63.5%, docs/normalization.md 2.8). This model used our own 60% (40–80%) before. The evaluator view uses the sheet's 100%. It overlaps partly with method 2, whose ideas already carry a yearly chance of success (2.5–40%): that is the chance an idea finds traction, this is the chance the organisation lasts to pursue it, so we apply it to both methods.

rows.label: If it fails: money it still moves, as a share of the successful case
rows.explainer: The shared success step's failure branch (facts: meta.failure_money_share, Ambitious Impact's 20%): a failed organisation still moves some money while it runs. Ambitious Impact's CEARCH sheet assumes success, so the evaluator view has none.

rows.label: If it fails: costs it still spends, as a share of the successful case
rows.explainer: A failed organisation spends for its first three years (facts: meta.failure_years_run) and then closes: CEARCH's own costs for those years over all five.

rows.label: Expected value over success and failure, on the successful benefit-cost ratio
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: the site's one success step for a new meta organisation (src/engine/moved-money.ts), the same as Better Futures Guide's: benefits and costs both take their expected value over success and failure. This model used to multiply benefits by the chance of success and charge all five years of costs to a failure as well.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers and advisers could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

Donations influenced per dollar of CEARCH's cost
rows.formula: (method1_weight * other_orgs_money_moved + method2_weight * avg(idea1_amount_moved, idea2_amount_moved, idea3_amount_moved) * (years_modelled - impact_delay_years)) / (method1_weight + method2_weight) / total_costs
rows.explainer: Donations influenced per dollar of CEARCH's cost (gross): what credit by share of resources counts as the donors' contribution (times the new-money share), the same formula as every meta model.

rows.label: Share of the outcome credited to CEARCH's cash budget
rows.explainer: The site's one formula for every meta charity (src/engine/moved-money.ts): with credit by share of resources on, the donors whose new money the organisation moves are contributors too, alongside staff's forgone pay, so the outcome is shared with them. Off, this is 100%.

Value of a dollar to global health and poverty charities (GiveWell's Top Charities, live), units of value
rows.explainer: GiveWell's four Top Charities (Against Malaria Foundation, Malaria Consortium's seasonal malaria chemoprevention, Helen Keller Intl's vitamin A, New Incentives), each at its result on this site under your values, weighted by what GiveWell directed to each in 2024 (50%, 29%, 18%, 4%).

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, units of value
rows.explainer: This organisation moves money only to global health and poverty charities, so a dollar moved is valued at that destination alone (GiveWell's Top Charities, live), not the across-causes mix.

rows.label: Share of money moved that is new money
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for every meta charity: about half the money moved wouldn't otherwise have been given (Ambitious Impact's Effective Giving Incubation report), from 35% to 80%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar you give
rows.explainer: Dollars of effective-donation value per dollar you give, each worth a dollar to global health charities at their live results: CEARCH's research and grants go to global health (hypertension and salt policy, lead, tobacco and alcohol taxes), so its dollars are valued there, not at the across-causes mix.
